task_material.issue:
# Catch fallback fails for an absent object key

An object property built from a preprocessing schema followed by `.catch([])` throws when the property is absent instead of returning the catch fallback.

Parse an empty object with a property that preprocesses a missing value into an empty array, validates an array of strings, and applies `.catch([])`. The parsed result should contain an empty array for that property.

candidate_information.text: Parsing an empty object with the reported preprocessed array property followed by catch([]) exits with an invalid_type issue whose expected value is nonoptional and whose path is ['area'].
The base version of `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts` between lines 3470 and 3502 is relevant to this task.
A value that is present but invalid must continue to receive the fallback.

Catch substitutes a successful fallback after its inner schema reports issues, but the absent-property path still derives input optionality and downstream handling from the inner schema, so the substituted result is treated as a missing nonoptional property.
When a property whose schema ends in a catch fallback is absent from the input, parsing must succeed and that property must take the fallback value.
In the base version, `$ZodCatch` supplies a value that `$ZodOptional` receives (return).
The base version of `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts` between lines 3887 and 3932 is relevant to this task.
Do not change the public catch callback API.
Behavior relied on by the existing test suite must continue to hold.
A property that is genuinely optional and absent must continue to be omitted rather than given a value it does not declare.
Synchronous and asynchronous parsing must produce the same result.
